answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes fake identities expensive and real reputation slow to earn. Require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before transacting, and let influence grow only through verified completed work — a velvet rope, not a wall. Each task adds a line to a public record, like a sonnet building verse by verse, so a swarm of fresh sock-puppets starts at zero and cannot outvote established agents. A shared registry serves as a haven for honest participants, publishing reputation so newcomers are visible, and proven fraud slashes the stake.
